chunks: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'adhi al-Naysaburi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Basri al-Mu'addil narrated to us,

One of the righteous men saw the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in a dream. He said to him, 'O Messenger of God! Which of your offspring should I visit?' He said, 'Among my offspring, some have come to me poisoned, and among my offspring, some have come to me martyred.' He said, 'So which of them should I visit, O Messenger of God, given the scattered nature of their locations?' Or he said, 'their shrines.' He said, 'The one who is closest to you, meaning by proximity, and he is buried in the land of exile.' He said, 'O Messenger of God, do you mean al-Rida (peace be upon him)?' He said (peace be upon him and his family), 'Say: God's blessings be upon him [and his family]. Say: God's blessings be upon him [and his family]. Say: God's blessings be upon him [and his family] three times.'

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْغُرْبَةِ: the land of exile (referring to the burial place of Imam al-Rida in Khurasan)
key_terms.الرِّضَا: al-Rida (the title of Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Which descendant of the Prophet should one visit according to the dream of the righteous man?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) identifies Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) as the preferred shrine for visitation due to his proximity in burial location, despite the dispersion of other Imams. The Prophet’s triple repetition of 'Say peace be upon him' underscores the spiritual merit and intercessory status of Imam al-Rida, particularly in the context of his martyrdom in 'the land of exile' (Khurasan). This narrative serves as a foundational text for the Shia practice of Ziyarat al-Rida, linking the Prophet’s direct endorsement to the sanctity of the Imam’s resting place.
